title: A line that begins with an absolute cd (cd "X" && …) is still placed where its shell started, or anywhere while another cd is pending, so it overlaps checks it cannot write under
outcome: A command whose line first changes to an absolute directory (`cd "X" && …`, `pushd "X" && …`) is placed only in X's worktree, whatever the shell's presumed position or a pending move of another command, so it no longer overlaps a check elsewhere, for the session's own checks and for other sessions'.
acceptance: A command whose line begins with `cd` or `pushd` to an absolute directory followed by `&&` is placed only in that directory's worktree, whether the shell is presumed elsewhere or another command's move is pending; tests cover both shapes from the field case, for the session's own open check.
A line whose first change is joined by `;` or `||`, a relative target, or a line TermAl cannot follow, keeps its current placement; tests cover each.
The full gate passed on the exact landed input.
